quote: Beweise, dass die Gl. 6ten Grades durch Wurzelzeichen niemals auf einen Parameter gebracht werden kann.
english: Prove that the equation of degree 6 can never be brought by means of radicals to one parameter.
topic: The page sketches how to show, without Riemann's integral, that the ξ-function has genus 1 as a function of t², asks whether the prime factors of Frobenius's group determinant are themselves determinants, and poses a problem on reducing the sextic equation by radicals to one or two parameters.

triage.modern_statement: Take the general degree-6 polynomial over C (or over Q, with coefficients as independent indeterminates). Show that no sequence of field extensions using only radicals, which in modern terms means Tschirnhaus transformations whose coefficients are built up by adjoining radicals, can turn it into a family of equations depending on just one essentially independent parameter. Put another way, at least two parameters are needed. If arbitrary algebraic functions are allowed instead of just radicals, this is Hilbert's 'Sextic Conjecture', rd_C(6) = 2: the sextic cannot be solved using algebraic functions of only one variable. Hilbert's note asks only about radicals, which is a weaker setting, so it is a variant of that conjecture.
triage.answered_by: Not answered. Hilbert published the closely related statement that the sextic needs 2 parameters, now called Hilbert's Sextic Conjecture, in 'Über die Gleichung neunten Grades' (Math. Ann. 97, 1927, p. 247). Brauer, Farb–Wolfson, Farb–Kisin–Wolfson, Reichstein and others treat it as still open. I found no source that settles the radicals-only version in the note.

evidence.claim: Farb–Wolfson list 'Hilbert's Sextic Conjecture' (RD = 2 for the general sextic), citing Hilbert 1927 p. 247. They describe it as part of Hilbert's conjecture that Hamilton's reduction of parameters for degrees 6, 7 and 8 is optimal, a question Brauer first stated precisely.
Hilbert's paper 'Über die Gleichung neunten Grades', Math. Ann. 97 (1927), 243–250, goes back to these parameter-reduction problems.
Wolfson (2020) says current methods 'cannot touch Hilbert's Sextic Conjecture (RD(6) = 2)'.
It is not known whether rd(n) > 1 for any n, so no lower bound has been proved even for the sextic.
Farb–Kisin–Wolfson use modern arithmetic techniques to reformulate the Sextic Conjecture as a statement that the resolvent degree of a particular cover equals 2.
Reichstein's survey says Hilbert asked whether rd_C(6) = 2 (the Sextic conjecture) alongside rd(7) = 3 (the 13th problem) and the octic case.

triage.why: The diary note matches Hilbert's later published claim that the general sextic cannot be reduced to one parameter, now the 'Sextic Conjecture' within the resolvent-degree program; it is not one of the 23 problems but is closely tied to the 13th. It remains open: nobody has shown rd(n) > 1 for any n. Researchers such as Farb, Wolfson, Kisin, Reichstein, Heberle and Sutherland are working actively on resolvent degree and essential dimension. Confidence is medium rather than high because the note restricts to radicals ('durch Wurzelzeichen'), while the published conjecture allows arbitrary algebraic functions. I found no source that addresses the radicals-only version specifically, so I am not claiming it is open; I am classifying it as the known open problem it most closely matches.
